data.title: Indian central bank lets rupee rise to break one-way bets on depreciation
data.description:
By Nimesh Vora and Ira Dugal

India's central bank is using the return of foreign inflows to break bets on a one-way slide in the rupee , allowing the currency to strengthen rather than buying dollars to rebuild reserves.

The strategy could encourage exporters to sell more dollars, reduce hedging by importers and ease foreign investors' concerns over currency losses, analysts and two sources familiar with the Reserve Bank of India's thinking said.

Indian equities have drawn a record $16 billion in foreign inflows in November, reversing nearly two years of selling and providing the central bank an opportunity to rebuild reserves.

Yet, the RBI has largely stayed out of the currency market despite an $80 billion drawdown in reserves from their $785.7 billion peak, following heavy dollar sales in October to defend the rupee as it approached its record low of 96.96 per dollar.

The RBI's dollar purchases during the rupee's recovery have been limited despite around $40 billion in forward commitments maturing over the next year, Dhiraj Nim, FX strategist and senior economist at ANZ Bank, said.

"We think its immediate priority is to put exporter hedging on a sustained footing and ease forward market imbalances (between importer and exporter hedging)," he added.

"That may require further rupee appreciation."

Nim said the rupee would face stiff resistance at 90-91 per dollar.

The currency closed at 92.99 on Friday.

The RBI is in "no hurry" to rebuild reserves and could allow the rupee to appreciate while replenishing reserves if inflows persist, one of the sources said, requesting anonymity due to restrictions on speaking to the media.

The strategy is consistent with Governor Sanjay Malhotra's publicly stated view that the rupee was undervalued.

An RBI spokesperson did not respond to an email seeking comment on the currency strategy.

EARLY SIGNS OF RESET

The rupee fell 4.8% in 2025 and another 5.5% in the first 10 months of this year, pressured by nearly $50 billion in foreign equity outflows amid India's limited exposure to the AI investment boom and steep valuations.

Persistent weakness prompted foreign investors to build short rupee positions in the offshore non-deliverable forwards market, exporters to retain dollar earnings and importers to step up hedging.

The resulting spiral prompted the RBI to curb open currency positions, impose reserve requirements on large hedging transactions and allow oil companies to buy dollars directly from its reserves.

With the rupee now up more than 4% from its lows, expectations are shifting.

Exporter hedging volumes over the past week were significantly higher than levels seen throughout the year, the head of markets at a large private-sector bank said, citing renewed hedging of future dollar receivables by Indian IT companies.

Investors turned bullish on the rupee for the first time in 18 months, helped by record foreign equity inflows and lower oil prices, a Reuters poll showed on Thursday.

FLEXIBILITY ON RATES

A sustained recovery in the rupee would provide the RBI higher flexibility to focus monetary policy on domestic growth and inflation conditions, rather than having to contend with currency weakness. This, in turn, could strengthen the rupee's fundamental support.

"Credible moves" on interest rates to address domestic sources of inflation would do more to ease underlying pressures on the rupee, said Aaron Hurd, senior portfolio manager for currency at State Street Investment Management.

"We need to see 2-3 more rate hikes over the coming quarters, preferably front-loaded with a hike at each of the next two meetings."

data.title: Rheinmetall's New Forecasts Likely Not Enough for Big Stock Rebound — Market Talk
data.description: Rheinmetall's move to downgrade sales and margin forecasts for the end of the decade might not be enough for the stock to rebound significantly, J.P. Morgan analysts write in a note. The German defense group's stock faced pressure in recent months, as order setbacks raised concerns among some investors that 2030 targets were too ambitious. The company now expects 2030 sales between 33 billion euros and 37 billion euros, down from prior guidance of about 50 billion euros, including contributions from acquisitions but excluding U.S. order wins. Its operating margin should come in at about 20%, compared with a prior forecast of more than 20%. Analysts say the sales target is a lot more credible now, but the new margin target still looks very ambitious. Rheinmetall shares trade 3.2% higher at 789.00 euros, but are down nearly 50% since January. (mauro.orru@wsj.com)

data.title: BOE Proposals Could Free Up Capital for Lloyds, NatWest — Market Talk
data.description: The Bank of England's proposal to lower CET1 capital requirements for U.K. banks might see Lloyds and NatWest eventually cut their common equity Tier 1 capital target ratios, UBS's Jason Napier and Sanjena Dadawala write. The proposals aim to increase the availability and cost effectiveness of credit and reassure investors of the international competitiveness of U.K. finance, UBS says. Buffer usability is unlikely to improve much because of the changes, the analysts say, but banks including Lloyds and NatWest could in time cut their common equity Tier 1 targets below the current 13% levels. For more internationally-active U.K. banks, the proposal is more important as a signal that domestic regulation is no longer tightening. Lloyds shares are up 1.2% while NatWest rises 1.4%. (michael.hennessey@wsj.com)

data.title: Arms Maker Rheinmetall Slashes Midterm Forecasts After Order Setbacks — Update
data.description:
By Mauro Orru

Rheinmetall lowered its sales and margin projections for the end of the decade, a sign that it doesn't expect to grow as strongly as it previously forecast after the German government canceled a big frigate order and delayed procurement of a lucrative combat-vehicle project.

The German defense group said its 2030 sales should come in between 33 billion euros and 37 billion euros, equivalent to a range between $36.20 billion and $40.58 billion. The company had previously expected 2030 sales of about 50 billion euros, a forecast that included contributions from acquisitions but excluded U.S. order wins.

Meanwhile, its closely watched operating margin should come in at about 20% at the end of the decade compared with a prior forecast of more than 20%. Its cash conversion rate is still expected above 50%.

The revisions show that Rheinmetall is moving to recalibrate expectations for the coming years following a number of setbacks in recent months that weighed on its stock and led some analysts to question whether its midterm targets were still achievable.

Rheinmetall shares in Frankfurt gained more than 3% on Friday, a sign investors viewed the lower forecasts as more attainable. Still, its stock has lost nearly half of its value since early January after the group slashed its 2026 guidance twice this year.

Last month, Rheinmetall flagged delays to Project Arminius, a large-scale German procurement of Boxer armored wheeled vehicles estimated by analysts to be worth over 12 billion euros. The company had anticipated a finalized contract by year-end, but now expects the project to be commissioned next year.

Despite the delay, Chief Executive Armin Papperger said the project size remained unchanged and that Arminius would start contributing to sales next year, with major prepayments expected upon contract signing.

In June, Berlin scrapped a roughly 15.2 billion-euro plan to buy six F126 frigates--a contract it had been transferring to Rheinmetall--citing delays and cost overruns with the initial contractor. Instead, the government opted to purchase eight MEKO A-200 frigates from German shipbuilder TKMS.

These setbacks mark a sharp reversal for a company that emerged as a premier beneficiary of surging defense budgets following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, as the North Atlantic Treaty Organization allies scrambled to replenish stockpiles depleted by weapons shipments to Kyiv.

Papperger said the opportunity for Rheinmetall hadn't disappeared. On Friday, the company secured an order valued at 738 million euros to supply Lynx combat vehicles to Romania. However, he said changes in orders had become more complex and frequent and that Rheinmetall needed to be more conservative in its forecasts and more agile to navigate a dynamic market.

data.title: BA, NOC, RTX Secured Billion-Dollar Deals This Week But One Defense Stock Stole The Limelight – A Look At This Week’s Contracts
data.description:
Key points:
  • RTX secured a $2.53 billion U.S. Navy contract for engine maintenance and support for F-35 fighter jets.
  • Northrop Grumman received a $1.13 billion award to develop three test aircraft under the Navy’s E-130J program.
  • Boeing signed a deal worth $2.82 billion with the U.S. Air Force to produce 15 KC-46A Pegasus aerial refueling aircraft, with production expected to be completed by June 2030.

Defense firms secured multi-billion-dollar military contracts over this truncated week, led by Boeing (BA), RTX (RTX) and Northrop Grumman (NOC), amid the Pentagon’s focus on increasing military aircraft production, but shares of Amentum (AMTM) gained the most on the back of two deals and a better-than-expected fourth-quarter bottom line.

Amentum secured a $68.3 million contract on Tuesday to support military communications operations. The company followed up Tuesday’s win by signing a $34.4 million Army contract modification for aviation maintenance services.

Amentum’s shares surged 20% after it reported Q4 earnings of $0.71 per share, beating Wall Street’s estimate of $0.66 per share, according to Fiscal.ai. The company reported a backlog of $48.3 billion. Earnings grew despite revenue declining 8% due to a 9% impact from an extra week in Q4 last year.

Boeing Bags Over $3B In Defense Deals

On Tuesday, Boeing secured a $2.82 billion Air Force contract modification to produce 15 KC-46A Pegasus aerial refueling aircraft. The production is expected to be completed by June 2030.

The aircraft allows military planes to refuel mid-flight, enabling them to operate over longer distances without landing.

On Monday, Boeing also received a $197.3 million contract modification to supply MH-47G helicopters to the U.S. Special Operations Command, with work expected to continue through September 2031.

RTX, Northrop Grumman Secure Billion-Dollar Navy Awards

RTX’s Pratt & Whitney received a $2.53 billion U.S. Navy contract to maintain F-135 engines that power F-35 Lightning II fighter jets. The contract covers repairs, engineering services, software maintenance, training and spare parts. The contract is valid till November 2027.

Northrop Grumman received a $1.13 billion contract modification from the U.S. Navy to develop three E-130J test aircraft. Work is expected to be completed by January 2030.

General Dynamics, Lockheed Martin Pick Up Navy Contracts

General Dynamics’ Bath Iron Works unit signed a $64.6 million contract with the Navy on Tuesday to provide support for Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyers, while Lockheed Martin secured two Navy contract modifications worth a combined $79 million for combat-system software integration and sonar systems.

Every stock in the cohort gained this week, with Amentum leading the pack with a 20.7% surge. Lockheed Martin gained 6%, Boeing 5.5%, General Dynamics 5.4%, Northrop Grumman 4%, and RTX 3.1%.

data.title: Bank of Japan official says stablecoins need reserve rules to preserve ‘singleness of money’
data.description:
Stablecoins require strict oversight of their backing assets and operational structures alongside carefully designed links to central bank money to prevent market fragmentation, Bank of Japan Executive Director Kazushige Kamiyama said on Friday.

Kamiyama said stablecoins and tokenized deposits are likely to coexist with other forms of digital money, but the resulting system will require safeguards.

“The challenge is to ensure that this diversity leads to a more efficient financial system without

creating unnecessary fragmentation or undermining financial stability,” he wrote in a speech delivered at an IMF seminar in Tokyo.

He said central bank money remains important as the settlement asset underpinning what the Bank for International Settlements calls the “singleness of money,” in which different forms of money denominated in the same currency remain exchangeable at par with finality.

Tokenization initiatives 

Kamiyama said the BOJ has launched a DLT Sandbox Project to examine use cases including cross-border payments, domestic interbank settlement, and cash settlement for tokenized Japanese government bonds.

Earlier this week, SBI Holdings, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, and the Solana Foundation began operations of SBI Solana Global, with stablecoin payments and financial asset tokenization among its stated areas of work.

Japan is also exploring a blockchain-based settlement system for stocks and Japanese government bonds, with a development plan expected in early 2027.

Kamiyama said the central bank is also participating in Project Agora, a BIS Innovation Hub project examining how tokenized commercial bank deposits and tokenized central bank money could operate on a shared platform for wholesale cross-border settlements.

data.title: CPTPP-ASEAN-EU meet: Stable trade, supply chain resilience in focus
data.description:
The European Union, the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) gathered in Vietnam to discuss economic ties and supply chain resilience.

Some of the 14 countries that were targeted with new U.S. tariffs this week were among the participants of the dialogue. These include the EU, Japan, Vietnam, Singapore, Thailand and Malaysia.

"In this time of global trade uncertainty, CPTPP parties and the EU are committed toreinforcing a stable and predictable trade environment," according to a joint statement from the blocs.

Notably, the EU and CPTPP announced a supply chain early warning network that aims to identify supply chain risks earlier, exchange information faster and coordinate responses to disruptions. The network will hold its first meeting in early 2027.

EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič said the network will help both blocs to "better anticipate disruptions, reduce vulnerabilities and support businesses and citizens who depend on open and reliable trade."

To note, the CPTPP is the successor to the Trans-Pacific Partnership, which was originally led by the U.S. President Trump withdrew from the Pacific Rim trade bloc in 2017.

The CPTPP now comprises the UK, Japan, Australia, Canada, Chile, Vietnam, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Singapore, Brunei and Peru.

Members of the CPTPP and ASEAN also resolved to strengthen supply chain resilience and global value chains through their collective actions, among other commitments.

Separately, the CPTPP agreed to start talks regarding the UAE, Indonesia ‌and the Philippines potentially joining the bloc.

data.title: Volkswagen drags rivals Mercedes, BMW into $1.2 billion India tax fight
data.description:
Key points:
  • Volkswagen says its India rivals also pay 10% duty on parts
  • Filing cites 2024 import data of BMW, Mercedes, Kia and others
  • Court to rule on Monday, likely only on whether 12-year look-back is allowed
  • Tariff investigations remain a sore point for foreign investors in India

By Aditi Shah and Aditya Kalra

Volkswagen has told an Indian court that tax authorities have wrongly singled it out over how it imports car parts at lower tariffs, alleging rivals Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Kia do the same, its latest salvo as it seeks to quash a $1.2 billion tax demand.

The German carmaker has been fighting since 2025 to quash the record tax demand over allegations it "deliberately" imported components at a 10% tariff and then assembled them into complete cars in India, evading the higher tariffs of around 30% applicable on car kits.

Volkswagen has denied the allegations, describing the case as a matter of "life and death" that could "wipe out" all of its investments in India, where it has just a 2% market share. The dispute coincides with the German carmaker's challenges back home due to worker disputes over pay, and falling sales in its key Chinese market.

After India accused VW of being the only carmaker indulging in such practices, the German company's unit in a non-public Mumbai court filing dated November 10 said "every manufacturer of comparable cars" follows the same "parts/components model" and pays duty at 10%.

If VW succeeds with its arguments about how its rivals import car parts, other carmakers could potentially face heightened scrutiny in the world's third-largest auto market.

TAX DEMAND 'DESERVES TO BE QUASHED'

"The contention that all other manufacturers paid duty at 30% while the petitioner alone paid 10% is unfortunate and factually incorrect," Volkswagen's India unit said in the filing, seen by Reuters, and being reported for the first time.

The tax demand "deserves to be quashed for requiring the petitioner alone to pay 30% duty while all other manufacturers pay 10%," it added.

To support its argument, VW attached a one-page table showing import shipment numbers of Mercedes , BMW, Hyundai's sister company Kia, Isuzu Motors and SAIC Motor's India unit JSW MG Motor, the filing showed.

VW's India unit, Skoda Auto Volkswagen India, declined to comment citing ongoing legal proceedings. Kia declined to comment on Volkswagen's submission, but said it imports car components in accordance with applicable laws.

The other rival carmakers it cited in the filing did not respond to Reuters queries, and neither did India's tax authorities.

In an October submission to the court, seen by Reuters, Indian tax authorities described VW's conduct as one of "fraud and subterfuge".

TARIFF DISPUTES LONG A SORE POINT FOR FOREIGN INVESTORS

Tariff disputes have long been a sore point for foreign investors in India, as investigations and lawsuits can drag on for years, triggering business uncertainty. Global liquor majors currently are sparring with New Delhi over the tariff rate on bulk Scotch imports, though Indian officials say they are only enforcing the law of the land.

In the VW dispute, India has alleged the carmaker shipped nearly complete Audi, Skoda and Volkswagen cars to its India plant but as individual parts and in separate consignments to avoid paying higher taxes applicable on car kits, and used internal software to manage such imports.

After VW initiated a court challenge months after receiving a tax demand in 2024, Indian authorities told the Mumbai judge that other carmakers were paying rightful duty on their parts imports.

VW SAYS IT IS BEING WRONGLY SINGLED OUT

VW is disputing that argument with its own analysis, its latest court filing showed.

BMW had 390,360 "major import shipments" of car components in 2024, while Mercedes had 80,972, all imported under the lower tariff rate category, VW said in its submission, without elaborating.

VW is of the view that such a high number of component imports by rivals are also then used to assemble cars, just like it does, and so the carmaker is being wrongly singled out by New Delhi, according to two people familiar with the matter.

However, a third person familiar with the dispute said for VW to succeed in its arguments, it will have to show that its rivals' imports were used to assemble complete vehicles.

The court in Mumbai will on Monday decide on Volkswagen's challenge, but the people familiar with the matter said it is likely the court will for now only rule on whether tax authorities could have gone back 12 years in scrutinising VW imports or not.

data.title: This investment strategist is 100% in cash - and warns that buying the Nasdaq dip is like catching a falling knife
data.description:
By Jules Rimmer

42 Macro strategist thinks the Fed is three moves away from neutral

A career spent catching knives will be a brief one, says 42 Macro's Darius Dale

Just because Nasdaq briefly entered bear-market territory this week, that's no reason in itself to buy stock, is the message from the head of one investment research service.

Darius Dale, founder and chief executive of the investment research boutique 42 Macro has advice for investors who think it is: "Research shows that if you try to make a career out of catching falling knives, you're not going to have a career for very long.'

For Dale, far better to "be the second investor in a confirmed trade, not the first in an unconfirmed."

Dale was articulating his extremely cautious opinions on the David Lin Report podcast, aired Thursday,. Opinions that are so cautious, his KISS model portfolio (standing for "Keep it Simple and Systematic") shifted into 80% cash at the end of September and has for the last few weeks actually been 100% cash.

Justifying this bearish stance he replied to Lin's suggestion that one might just buy stocks because they've declined so much, "that's just not what we do. We have a risk management system that's looking for signals to confirm" a move like that.

The main reason for Dale's extreme caution is that the Federal Reserve, for credibility's sake, needs to hike in December, and probably again in March to shore up its inflation-fighting credentials. "If they don't hike in December, they might as well close the institution," he says. Right now, Dale's models calculate the Fed is three 25-basis point hikes away from a policy that could be described as neutral.

The Fed is expected to tighten into the first half of 2027

It's not just inflation forcing rates higher. Dale's Wall Street contacts indicate to him that the hyperscalers (AMZN) (GOOG) (MSFT) may issue as much as $1 trillion in debt over the next few years, triple what they raised this year. That adds upward pressure on the cost of capital.

Dale cites many factors suggesting the economy is running too hot, highlighting supercore personal consumption expenditure at 4.2% year-over-year. It may take then, in Dale's opinion, until the second half of 2027 for the narrative to shift from a restrictive to a more accommodative approach, creating a policy tailwind to support equities, metals and bitcoin (BTCUSD).

As well as its KISS model, 42 Macro also runs a "Dr Mo" portfolio, representing a discretionary risk management overlay that interprets signals from 80 different factors, including rates, currencies, stocks and commodities. Late September, that model too suggested a reduction in beta - stocks that exaggerate market moves in any direction - and to move up the quality spectrum.

Dale is concerned that markets are having to digest a slowdown in the artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout, specifically identifying data centers as well as the situation with Nvidia (NVDA) and issues surrounding its chip sales. Yet, he observes earnings forecasts for 2027 are still at or near the cycle highs.

At some point, when markets are convinced about the direction of rates, the markets may well rip, Dale says and when they do the things to buy will be semiconductors SOX, Korea KR:180721, Taiwan XX:180909, base metals , bitcoin and other crypto currencies. For now, though, "the signals are not telling us to put on risk."

-Jules Rimmer
